title: 3D Rendering Services: Product and Architectural | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering services for photoreal product shots, packaging, campaign visuals and interiors, plus 3D models for web and ads, delivered on agreed dates.
h1: 3D rendering services for products, packaging and spaces
intro: 22 Signals provides 3D rendering services for companies that need photoreal images before, or instead of, a photo shoot: product renders, packaging, campaign visuals, interior and architectural visualization, and 3D models for websites and ads. You send drawings, CAD files or references, and we deliver finished images and models on dates agreed in writing.

sections.h: Why companies render instead of shooting
p: A photo shoot needs the finished product, a studio, a photographer, props and a date. If the product is still in production, comes in twelve colors, or will change packaging next quarter, the shoot becomes the bottleneck for the whole launch.

A 3D render needs a good model and good lighting. Once the model exists, a new color, angle, background or season is a new render, not a new shoot. That is why brands use renders for catalogs, product pages, crowdfunding campaigns, pitch decks and ads long before stock arrives.
The same logic applies to buildings and interiors. A developer selling homes off plan, or a designer pitching a fit-out, needs buyers to see the space before it exists.

Packaging is a common starting point. A new box or bottle design can be rendered from the print dielines before a single unit is made, so the team can judge it on shelf, in a hand or in an ad, and buyers and retailers can see it in a pitch. When the design changes, the render changes with it.

Campaign visuals are the other end of the scale: one or two hero images built to carry a launch across ads, the website, email and print. Here the scene, the light and the mood matter as much as the product, so we agree references and a rough composition before any final rendering starts.

p: Good product renders live or die on materials. Brushed metal, frosted glass, soft-touch plastic, fabric and skin-care textures each catch light differently, and buyers notice when a render looks like plastic pretending to be something else. We build materials from your samples, swatches or reference photos and test them under the lighting used for the final images.

We also keep scale and detail honest. A render that makes a product look bigger or more premium than it is will cost you in returns and reviews. Each image is checked against the real product or the drawings before delivery.

For real estate developers, architects, interior designers and fit-out companies we create still images and short flythroughs of spaces that are not built yet. We work from plans, elevations, sections and material schedules, and agree camera angles with you before rendering so the images show what buyers and planning audiences care about.
The model can be reused across marketing: brochure images, website galleries, hoarding boards, social posts and a walkthrough video from our animation team.

sections.h: How a rendering project runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we look at what you have, what the images are for and how many you need. A single hero shot and a 200-variant catalog are very different jobs.
Plan: a shot list, camera angles, style references and a schedule with a delivery date for each batch, in writing.
Build: modeling, materials, lighting and a first set of draft renders for comment. After your feedback we produce the final high-resolution images, plus any crops and sizes listed in the plan.
Grow: the models are kept ready, so new colors, products or campaign scenes can be added later without starting again.

faqs.a: 3D rendering services turn a digital 3D model into finished images that look like photographs. The model is built from CAD files, drawings or photos, given realistic materials and lighting, and rendered from chosen angles. Companies use them for product pages, packaging, ads, catalogs and property marketing, often before the real product or building exists.

faqs.q: Can renders really look like photos?
faqs.a: Yes, when the model, materials and lighting are done properly. Many of the product images you see online for electronics, cosmetics and furniture are renders. The details that give a render away are usually materials and scale, which is why we build materials from real references and check every image against the product or drawings before delivery.

faqs.q: Do we need CAD files to get started?
faqs.a: No, but they help. CAD gives exact proportions, so modeling is faster and more accurate. Without CAD we can model from technical drawings, or from photos of a sample with measurements. We tell you after the first look which route your project needs, and how it affects the schedule.

faqs.q: How long does a product render take?
faqs.a: It depends on the model, the materials and the number of images, and we confirm the delivery date in writing during planning. A single product from clean CAD on a studio background moves fastest. Lifestyle scenes, many variants and complex materials take longer. Once the model exists, new angles and colors are much quicker.

faqs.q: Do you do architectural rendering for real estate?
faqs.a: Yes. We create exterior and interior images and short flythrough videos for developers, architects, interior designers and agents, working from plans, elevations and material schedules. Camera angles are agreed before rendering. The images suit brochures, websites, hoarding boards and social, and the same model can become a walkthrough animation.

The number of review rounds is set in the written scope, so there are no surprises. Most projects have a round on draft renders, where angles, materials and lighting are adjusted, and a round on the finals. Changes to the product itself, such as a new design, are scoped separately because they mean remodeling rather than adjusting.

faqs.q: Why choose 3D rendering services over a photo shoot?
faqs.a: Choose renders when the product is not finished, comes in many variants, or will change soon, and when you want the same look across hundreds of images. Choose a shoot when real people, real places or real texture are the point. Many brands use both: renders for product pages and variants, photography for people and lifestyle.

faqs.q: Can we use the 3D models on our website?
faqs.a: Yes. We can prepare lighter versions of the models for interactive 3D viewers and, where your platform supports it, augmented reality, so shoppers can rotate a product or see it in their room. Web models need to load quickly, so we optimize them separately from the high-detail versions used for still renders.
